editor_note: A quiet weekend edition: federal cannabis registrations under Schedule III reshape a high-risk sector, DOJ pursues crypto and money-laundering cases, and Europe debates where AI safety oversight should live.

bottom_line.text: DEA begins registering medical marijuana dispensaries; reassess cannabis-sector KYC and vendor risk policies.
Nomad Bridge hacker extradited; review digital-asset smart-contract controls and tracing capabilities.
Smuggling and asylum-fraud laundering ring sentenced; refresh related AML monitoring typologies.

cards.title: Justice Department Announces Federal Registrations for Medical Marijuana Dispensaries
cards.summary: The DEA is moving forward with the initial issuance of hundreds of federal registrations to qualifying state-licensed medical marijuana dispensaries, under the Attorney General's order implementing Schedule III controls for certain medical marijuana activities.
cards.impact: Banks, payment processors, landlords and vendors serving cannabis businesses should revisit risk appetite, KYC and federal registration checks as Schedule III controls take effect.

cards.title: Israeli National Extradited to Face Charges Over $2.89M Nomad Bridge Crypto Heist
cards.summary: Alexander Gurevich, 49, appeared in the Northern District of California on a 2023 indictment alleging he exploited the Nomad Bridge smart contract to steal $2.89 million in virtual currency.
cards.impact: Firms handling digital assets should test smart-contract and bridge controls and confirm their monitoring can trace and freeze stolen crypto flows.

cards.title: Cuban Nationals and Florida Man Sentenced in Smuggling, Asylum Fraud and Money Laundering Conspiracy
cards.summary: Five Cuban nationals and one U.S. citizen were sentenced for their roles in a vast conspiracy involving alien smuggling, asylum fraud and money laundering.
cards.impact: AML teams should keep human-smuggling and fraud-proceeds typologies in transaction monitoring scenarios and suspicious-activity reporting training.

cards.title: Austria Pitches Vienna as Home for a United Nations AI Security Centre
cards.summary: Austria is proposing Vienna as the site of a UN AI security centre while governments continue to debate how to respond to global concerns over AI safety.
cards.impact: AI governance leads should watch for emerging international AI safety bodies that may shape standards alongside the EU AI Act.

cards.title: Court Rules Navy Not in Violation of Clean Water Act Over Pearl Harbor-Hickam Fuel Releases
cards.summary: A federal court in Hawaii ruled after a bench trial that the U.S. Navy is not violating the Clean Water Act, citing its response to 2020 and 2021 fuel releases and improvements to fueling infrastructure.
cards.impact: Environmental compliance teams can note that documented remediation and infrastructure upgrades weighed heavily in defeating Clean Water Act claims.

cards.title: THE HACK: EU Targets Quantum Sovereignty
cards.summary: Euractiv's tech policy newsletter reports on EU moves toward quantum sovereignty, alongside AI safety, social media bans and network fees.
cards.impact: Security and tech-policy teams should track EU quantum and digital sovereignty plans that may later shape procurement and encryption requirements.
